questions.title: Fixed Columns Cap Relationship
questions.question:
A teammate wrote this schema for a blog, where one post can have many comments:

```sql
CREATE TABLE posts (
    id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(255),
    comment_1 VARCHAR(500),
    comment_2 VARCHAR(500),
    comment_3 VARCHAR(500)
);
```

What is the main problem, and what's the correct fix?

options.optionText: A fixed number of comment columns caps the relationship — create a separate comments table with a post_id foreign key instead
id should not be declared as a primary key
title should be split into two columns
The comments should be merged into one column separated by commas

questions.title: Junction Table Enrollment Count
questions.question:
Given this SQL:

```sql
CREATE TABLE students (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(255));
CREATE TABLE courses (id INT PRIMARY KEY, title VARCHAR(255));

CREATE TABLE enrollments (
    id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    student_id INT,
    course_id INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (student_id) REFERENCES students(id),
    FOREIGN KEY (course_id) REFERENCES courses(id)
);
```

Current rows in enrollments: (1, 1, 1), (2, 1, 2), (3, 2, 1) (columns: id, student_id, course_id)
How many courses is the student with id = 1 enrolled in?

To ensure every table has exactly the same number of columns
To turn every relationship into a many-to-many relationship

questions.title: Duplicated Customer Data Fix
questions.question:
A teammate wrote this schema for an orders system:

```sql
CREATE TABLE orders (
    id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_name VARCHAR(255),
    customer_email VARCHAR(255),
    product VARCHAR(255)
);
```

There's already a separate customers table storing customer details. What's wrong with this design, and what's the fix?

options.optionText: Nothing is wrong — storing the name and email directly avoids extra joins
product should be split into product_name and product_price
id should not be declared as a primary key since orders can repeat
customer_name and customer_email duplicate data that already lives in customers — replace both with a single customer_id foreign key instead
